clue.text: Able to move supply and perhaps arm monarch

parts.note: an arm is one example of a limb
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina, used in crosswords for a monarch or queen

explanation.surface: A supply chain that can shift, and perhaps arm the king, sounds like a war plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like the noun for provisions, but it is the adverb 'in a supple way', part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can move supply is flexible and lithe, the synonym being supple of body.

clue.text: Writer contributing to stories, say, I study

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A writer adds to a collection of stories while studying.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who composes short prose pieces is one kind of author or penman.

clue.text: Tailored trenchcoat for scientific expert

indicators.note: tailored means cut and refitted, so the letters of the coat word are made over into a new order

explanation.surface: A boffin wears a made-to-measure raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A technocrat is a technical specialist given power, a scientist or engineer in government.

clue.text: Position that's not ethical in test breaking up friendship

indicators.note: breaking up means the word for friendship is split apart so another piece sits in its middle

parts.note: amity is friendship or goodwill
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: An unprincipled stance shows itself when an exam ruins a friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance with no moral principles at all is the condition of being without ethics.

clue.text: Something players try to avoid in club, for example

definitions.meaning: footballers try not to be shown a yellow or red one by the referee
clubs is one of the four suits in a pack, so a club is one of these

explanation.surface: Players in a club try to avoid something.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a booking is shown on one, and a club is a playing piece from the pack.

clue.text: Parking, say, in golf club

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
to say something is to utter it

explanation.surface: Parking at a golf club is the topic.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the flat-faced club a golfer uses on the green to roll the ball into the hole.

clue.text: Lied when corruptly generating capital

indicators.note: corruptly suggests something twisted out of its proper form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lied out of corruption, making money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money in this surface, but it is a seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the seat of government of India, so it is a capital city.

clue.text: Test cricket, for instance, accommodating minimal change

indicators.note: accommodating means taking something in, so one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: a cricket is one example of an insect
P is a penny, the smallest coin and so the least change

explanation.surface: A Test match of cricket that sees little change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test cricket' reads as the sport's international match; split, 'Test' is the definition and the cricket is the chirping creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something closely for faults is to test or scrutinise it.

clue.text: Removal of this large plant makes street shorter

indicators.note: removal of this says the answer's letters sit within the word that follows and can be lifted out of it
makes ties the lifting out to its result, the word that follows becoming smaller
shorter says that what remains is the short form ST, so the answer is the run of letters taken from inside

explanation.surface: Felling a big plant makes a road look shorter.
explanation.walkthrough: Lift the letters of the plant out of 'street' and ST is left, the usual abbreviation for street, so the street is literally shorter.
explanation.definitionFit: A large woody plant with a trunk and branches is the oak or elm kind of growth.

clue.text: Quantify average cut with certainty

indicators.note: cut means the word for average is docked, losing its final letter

parts.note: the mean is the average
sure means certain, done with certainty

explanation.surface: Someone wants the cut in the average put in numbers for certain.
explanation.definitionFit: To quantify something is to gauge its size or amount.

clue.text: A head we encountered in pub in holiday gear

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the word for pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a head, as in a price per head, means each
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chief we met in the pub was dressed for the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A head' looks like a person in charge; it is 'per head', each.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing for the seaside, such as swimsuits and shorts, is gear worn on holiday.

clue.text: Unfashionably old saw

definitions.meaning: to see someone is to go out with them romantically

explanation.definitionFit: Something out of fashion is passé, and someone who saw another romantically was courting them.

clue.text: When provoked, one may charge cash

definitions.meaning: a big horned animal that charges when angered

explanation.definitionFit: The horned beast of Africa charges if provoked, and in old British slang the word also means money.

clue.text: Textual error in a line at end of American volume

indicators.note: at end of says the article and line go after the volume word

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of the metric volume

explanation.surface: A misprint in a line at the end of a book from the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' looks like a book, but it is a measure of capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, a misprint or typo is called by this name, the error being in the letters.

clue.text: In speculative activity, one is right, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the words might be arranged another way, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A speculator thinks they may be right.
explanation.definitionFit: Forming hypotheses without proof is the activity of speculation.

clue.text: Short excerpt from substantial amount of information heard

parts.note: sound means solid, substantial

indicators.note: heard means the information unit is spoken, giving a word said the same way

parts.note: a byte is a unit of computer information

explanation.surface: A short clip taken from a big amount of data that was listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief clip of speech taken from a longer piece, as used by broadcasters, is a short excerpt.

clue.text: Scrambled jet, tho' under fire, in sci-fi movie

indicators.note: scrambled, like a jet sent up in a hurry, also means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fighter jet takes off fast under fire in a science-fiction film.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter Jed signs the puzzle with this Star Wars title.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the 1983 third Star Wars film, a science-fiction picture.

clue.text: Two-wheeled vehicle putting strain on writer

parts.note: to rick a joint is to strain or sprain it
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A vehicle puts pressure on an author.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled cart pulled by a person is a vehicle of Asia.

clue.text: Badly misshape? It's stress

indicators.note: badly suggests the word is formed wrongly, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Something shaped badly causes anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stress' looks like worry, but it is emphasis in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Special importance or force placed on a word is stress or accent.

clue.text: With maximum possible speed, move fast to discipline

parts.note: c is the symbol for the speed of light, the fastest anything can go
to hasten is to hurry

explanation.surface: Move at top speed to punish someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise or rebuke someone is to discipline them.

clue.text: Get out or in

definitions.meaning: to step down from a train or bus
a fire that is still in is still burning

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the British sense of a fire still burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers step off a vehicle when they get out, and something burning or lit is on fire.

clue.text: Counter in bank holding page

indicators.note: holding means the word for bank keeps the page piece within it

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A shop counter in a bank holds a page.
explanation.definitionFit: To counter an argument is to answer or respond to it.

clue.text: Joining army, finally agreeing

indicators.note: finally means just the last letter of the word army is taken

parts.note: okaying, or OK-ing, is agreeing to something

explanation.surface: Enlisting in the army, finally consenting.
explanation.definitionFit: To yoke two things is to couple or link them, as oxen under one beam.

clue.text: Learner in academic stream still

indicators.note: in says the learner piece is placed within the river

parts.note: the Cam is the river flowing through the university city of Cambridge
L is the learner driver plate

explanation.surface: A student in a university's river is motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that is still is placid and unruffled.

clue.text: Unfriendly second row

parts.note: a tiff is a row, a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A second quarrel leaves things frosty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a line, but it rhymes with cow: a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal, cold, unbending manner is unfriendly.

clue.text: Fiercely criticise fallacy, oddly enough

indicators.note: oddly says the letters in odd positions of the word are picked

explanation.surface: Someone is savaged for a mistaken idea, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: To skin someone, figuratively, is to attack them harshly in words.

clue.text: Prohibits discussion about European epitome of rapid growth

indicators.note: about means the word for prohibits goes round the European piece

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit
talk is discussion

explanation.surface: Someone bans talk about Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jack and the Beanstalk the plant shot up overnight, the classic example of fast growth.

clue.text: Fighting about hard time getting across

indicators.note: about means the fighting phrase is wrapped round the hard piece

parts.note: a country fighting is at war
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A battle about tough times is crossing over.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word means crosswise, from one side to the other, so across.

clue.text: People improperly taken into state

parts.note: men are people

indicators.note: improperly means the word into is put in a wrong order, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: People wrongly taken into a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a nation, but it is the verb to say.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer to or bring up something is to state or note it.
